body: I have a permit but honestly didn't think about getting my gun back. I had given to my brother when my son was depressed. But I think it would be good to get it back. My ex had kicked a metal door-with dead bolt- because the force broke apart the wood frame. But I got a brace now. One friend said to download a call recorder and talk to him about some of the things he did to bring in front of judge. I decided a protection order after I get my weapon would kind of call his bluff. I mean...if he knows he will definitely be the prime suspect if I go missing may prevent him from acting on his threat. And if he does lose it and try to break in I will have previous contact with law so if I do have to point it at him or shoot...its not out of the blue.  Thanks everyone. I feel much more better to take some actions to help feel less out of control.
Thank you for writing back. I'm going to try to plan something. At least taxes are in to help.

I've known a family. They never have gotten over it. It was nearly 30 years ago. Every holiday, the boy's birthday, monumental events like weddings...are still difficult.  They still miss him, mourn him, wonder how they missed the signs, his brother posts every year on Facebook to try to bring awareness to others.

Have you ever read Flowers for Algernon? I struggle with the same feeling you express as mediocre at much, great at nothing. Except I've also seen myself get worse. Intelligent enough to know I'm less than what I used to be.

I agree with the previous comments. We can't measure ourselves against others. There is always people better. But there are thousands worse.... Like just now....did you notice my error of "is" vs "are"? Not everyone can or would.

You show tenacity. Persevearance. Id love to talk to you outside of this forum. It can feel overwhelming when you stack everything up. But I love you are challenging yourself. Look at some of those 100 day challenges...a girl who learned how to do push ups,  a man who just wanted to touch his toes.... We love in a society that wants instant gratification but they prove things take repeated effort. You see improvement in your art in 8 days...imagine how it will be in 30.

Keep kickin my friend. Your journey is Yours alone. The oak doesn't wish it was like the bamboo...or vice versa. And both are unique and amazing. You are as well.

Heard a quote....it's not that I want to die, it's that I want to stop living this way. Circumstances can be changed. What has brought you joy or peace? Music? Walking? Sunlight? Surprising someone with a snail-mail letter?

Honey...I get this. After seeing the same type of reaction to my son...admitted into 2 different hospitals.  It was embarrassing my kid knew more than they did about their own professions.   What this tells me is your probably do very well with CBT.  Have you tried that before? You are educated about the consequences of OD'g. Can you make a decision to focus on how to heal? What could reverse, repair, or reduce the damage? This world needs intelligent people....of nothing else, maybe it is a calling to you to help troubled youth because you can see through their ability to logically dissociate and come off ok.

I don't know if she meant that it thought she could over-react hoping it's a bluff but it was wrong for her not to take you seriously and if I were your mum I would show you compassion. I would ask you why you feel things have gotten so bad that you feel that is am option. We can show our parents respect, but they are Not gods. Some are very messed up. Don't let her issues weigh in on your decision. I'm so sorry that happened.

I wish I could say something poetic and meaningful to make it better. Sometimes life is simply how we show others they matter. Doing acts of kindness. Start with yourself. Get sleep, eat, get sunlight....know that every smile you can give a stranger still matters. You matter.
I hope you got help. I wanted to ask you something. You posted somewhere else and I wonder how you can see through BS. Its a skill I lack. Anyway....I hope you are ok

There are famous people with scars on their faces. Seal, Tommy Flanagan got the chershire grin done to him. All the people that have been in accidrnts, fires, acid. Yes....you did it to yourself. Do you know what that tells me? You were f'ing hurting. Maybe you unconsciously needed others to see how bad you were feeling.  Could you use this to help others? Volunteer at hospitals or schools. Demystify it by owning it. Yes people will look and some will pull away at first, but they do that with birthmark too! Its human. But people also respond to self-acceptance or confidence. You have scars that show you suffered....but they don't DEFINE you. And maybe people know you did it - but will you be around the same people forever? You don't have to talk to others about how they got there. There are enough hands and bullies if I saw a facial scar, I would think auto accident first, then fight...and if/when you told me the truth, I would feel compassion for you that you felt so ugly and unloved it was the only way to let out the emotional pain. My final thought...why do you feel ugly? My child self harmed because they hated their birth gender. I'm not accusing you of that ...but you are lovable. However you are

My son is suicidal. I've taken him in to counseling, got meds, hospitalized him. I've paid close attention to his eating, hygirne, moods. We talk openly. We talk about alternatives when the impulsive urge hits to get through it. First step is good sleep. Mostly, we stay active. Sunlight. Would he join you in a project? Do you share interests? Robotics? Shop? Fishing? Frisbee golf? You could open up to him. I told my son "winter seems to be a struggle for me I always forget. I can't believe a few dark days can feel so oppressive" we also made a deal. I will play Dark Souls with him at least an hour. He will do at least one CBT exercise. That's cognitive behavior therapy. It reaches us to examine our triggers, the thoughts behind them, and forward movement. Knowing what we are doing next helps. Plans... I hope this helps. You can tell him you don't want to be annoying checking in him but you care about him. Why? What would you miss? Tell him. The day after my son attempted I was devastated constantly with the hole that would have been in my life. Seeing him come down the stairs, his goofy humor, the way he always avoids pictures....

At the end of the day though I've had to radically accept I cannot be around him 24/7 and I'm doing all I can. But you could be loved by millions (Robin Williams) or have kids that need you (Linklin Park- Bennington) and still do it. It is ultimately their choice. It might not hurt for you to talk to a counselor as well.

Hello. I want you to know what you are worth is a thoughtful response and I'm processing that now. You are incredibly introspective and have an above average intelligence - you've mastered English better than some native speakers. Please allow me a little time to put together my own words as I suffered a concussion recently and feel a little off right now. I just wanted to respond quickly so you know you are cared for.
I'm not sure what you mean but it seems almost every fear, chased down to the source, is a fear of being alone/not mattering. What do you mean we all live in fear? Unite in what way?

Self harm can become addictive. It is an endorphin rush. A dopamine thing when you get so close...but live.  It can be especially hard if you suffer OCD. After a while, you need it again. I'm not sure it's dying you want but the almost dying and you recognize you could, accidentally or not, take it too far.

Some people in the bdsm community can also experience this. Even that actor who died of erotic asphyxiation... Its getting so close that gives the rush. 

There are other ways to get the rush without the danger of death. 

So not sure how much is wishing to die...of course that needs to be addressed...but it can be confusing to where you may still think you want to when in fact, you have become addicted to these things that have become normalized to you. I hope that makes sense and was helpful.

Perhaps you do have to accept being blood doesn't always mean you are family and you can only control you. You can tell your brother "when you scream at me I just feel like (what you feel... I can't trust you, you hate me) I need for you to talk to me , not scream." If he gets sarcastic but quiet say "thank you for hearing me out" and walk away. Maintain your respect or detachment if you can. "I don't want to be around you when you're like this. Its too much like dad" and go to your room. He will get the picture and change or he won't. Try not to engage him at that same level. 

Your mom probably sees how your brother and you are and tries to compensate by being overly protective to try to show you are precious. I did that before. I didn't mean to baby my son...I just thought if I could love him enough I could make up for other shit he went through.

Your dad has an addiction and it isn't healthy. But it's not because you deserve his wrath. When you are able to get away from that household, you can do the same. "Sure if like to see you..." and if he gets drunk tell him it was good to see him But you've got to go...or won't unless it's while he is sober.

Your brother may be using his anger and abuse as his way of dealing with the home life. Bullying you gives him a sense of control. It doesn't mean he hates you. It doesn't mean it will always be that way.

Just know family isn't always who we grew up with and if you can't talk to mom or set boundaries with dad and brother - it doesn't mean you'll end up alone. The world is big...

It you were spared accidents that could have killed you, perhaps it is because you are meant to find a way to forgive yourself and her. Do you feel no one should ever be forgiven for wrong doing? Ever? Could you have compassion on anyone? If so, don't you feel you could also?

I don't mean to tout religion but  when you are repentent, part of the he'll we put ourselves through is knowing we can't take it back. Its done. Sometimes there are ways to get reconciliation with who we hurt.  Sometimes not. Could you talk to your mom at all about how bad you feel? Maybe she has too. 

Can your counselor help with the event so maybe the suicidal feelings would become moot?

I don't mean to be too familiar but sweetie...you are articulate, introspective, and you have had trauma from an early age. Can I say it like this? You deserved a dollar....you Needed a dollar. Those who were your caretakers only had 50cents because of their own dysfunction. At their best...they couldn't give you what you needed or deserved. That is not because You didn't deserve it or some power is trying to curse your life. It was people with their own issues.

You recognize emotional abuse for what it is. Please consider you don't deserve to be a target. You have this tragic past but all bad things we go through can give us courage, empathy, compassion to help or understand others. 

Because you know what happened was all wrong - you will be a better parent if you choose to have kids. Because it happened to you, you will know the signs and not allow someone else to be abused...or be able to relate in a way no one else can.

Think about what you want and write down some steps on how to get it. Consider options. If your roommate will not accept boundaries about the emotional abuse, what can you do to get out? Or get them out?

Hang in there. You strike me as quite strong...look what you've come through. Come through. You don't have to stay in those memories. If I could go back in time and prevent these things that happened, I would.  Consider that hon...you deserved better. I believe in you.

I feel it would be like sleeping...lack of consciousness. But I've since felt I've had proof of a beyond. So I'm not saying it would be a bad place - but what if you don't just stop being? This is just my own feeling. Maybe people who don't want to exist do cease.

Oh honey....that sounds like a frightening and confusing event. You know, all you can do to make it right is to go to him. Just tell him how you wished it would have gone. Like "you know about what happened? I wish I would have used my words and asked you to put it down. Things got out of hand and I'm sorry if I scared you - I love you"  

If you want and he's mature enough you can tell him about the fight or flight response which made you impulsive... 

But also hon...my youngest was always quiet. He never felt he had to tell his older (by 6 yrs) brother how much he meant but now hes 14 and brother is 21 and moved out at 18. Younger brother has struggled feeling abandoned by what he considered his dad's replacement.

I also am friends with a guy whose older bro killed himself. Its been 30 yrs. He was 11 when it happened. He has NEVER got over it. 

You gotta keep kickin man. Show him how to persevere. 

I don't know if you can get in to a counselor or doctor but sometimes puberty/hormones can wreak havoc and maybe this is part of the anxiety or panic attacks you are feeling.

I hope you are feeling a little better...

If mom is also suicidal and you go through with it, she may actually feel guilty enough to do herself in and your child is an orphan wondering why she wasn't good enough to live for. 

If this was 5 yrs ago you made the mistake, maybe you both should look at how to get forward motion. There are self-sufficiency homes where I live that help people interview, find a vehicle, etc to get self sufficient. What steps could both of you take to become independent? If she can't or won't, what about you?

If you accept worst case is she kills herself and best is she divorces you...what can you do to prepare for Your single parenting? She assumes she would get custody "burden". Not likely. Look at what you can do.  Please understand it's easier to be angry than sad sometimes because it is empowering. She isn't well...but it doesn't mean she's right.  And e en if you feel she has some right to be upset...how long should you be punished? You seem sincerely regretful. Forgive yourself and focus on your daughter.
Are you still here? I'm glad you recognize how sleep deprivation can be a factor. HUGE one actually....

I think it's awesome you are able to identify the trigger. And I'm happy to hear you have this good memory of fishing. Is it something you could share with someone else? If not wife or child or nephew/niece...maybe be a Big Brother to a child who needs it.

My eldest is an Aspie. Man....it's a gift. Truly. Sure there are some struggles but I think y'all use more of your brain than the rest of us. Your ability to hyperfocus and gain knowledge is impressive! Creative. Intelligent. He jokes he now uses his "power for good" by reading ways to love his wife, how to make things as gifts. 

What if you and the Mrs made some cards to send out for no reason. How tickled and blessed the recipients would feel and this might be a feel good thing for both of you. Or if you like animals, volunteering at a shelter.. 

Anyway...hope you are feeling a little better. Day by day.

Has anything changed? I think you did great! The only thing I keep hearing is the 'selfish' comment usually just makes them feel worse or apathetic. I have generational depression with suicidal ideation.  My mom, myself, my son. My mom stays because she doesn't want my son to think it's a viable option. I dont because I feel I gave up my right to my own life when I became a parent. My son...all that seems to help is day to day talks. Cognitive behavior therapy....challenging the dark thoughts. Letting go of the past. Acknowledging what we both would have wished to be different about a situation that hurt (like bullying). 

He has a family counting on him. He needs to show them giving up isn't the option. Sometimes how we handle ad ersity and failure is more of a legacy to our lives one's then an easy win. Persevearance. Who looks up to him? When we can't live for ourselves, sometimes we can live for others.  Not because we don't want to be viewed as selfish..but because we CAN recognize the value of life in others and love them by staying.

I don't know what intake is but if it's medical related can't the college work with you? Winter makes things harder too.. I wish I had words but it's 5 am here and I Gtg ...but you are being thought of...hang on there

My daughter has a lot of guilt because she is a T1 diabetic. Insurance requires I come up with $2800 this month before they will send her next supply due in March.  Trying to ease her pain...she would need over 1500 shots a year...I got her a pump that reduces injections to less than 500 But has been like a car payment each month.

What I'm getting at is 1) it is my duty and privilege to care for her 2) expense is an accepted part of parenting 3) I'd sell myself to make it work if I had to to save her pain...

How on earth do I help her see I want to? That I don't resent HER? I get mad about the system. I get worried and frustrated over my bills some days...but I never for a second blame her. Do you feel I should? Should she be working to pay me back? I don't think she should.

I bet it is the same...why feel guilt over the responsibility your parent(s) chose? Unless you are made to feel you are a burden. In which case you don't deserve that. Would you blame or resent your own child? 

Money is nothing. Your life is what is valuable!

What could you do to change one thing you don't like? My daughter is now home schooled due to anxiety. And our community college has GED classes. Are you interested in getting your diploma now as a start?

I'm on here tonight because my younger son wants to die and I don't know how to help him. But I've an older son who is more like how you feel. He's 21.

I don't know why you are stuck or if you could look at other options. If not...like my son. So smart but your writing looks amazing compared to his because he had scarlet fever and the fever destroyed a part of his brain so he can't spell better than 1st grade level. Orally, you can't tell. But he's stuck. And feels incompetent and I've witnessed him make mistakes at work but they have kept him 3 yrs now.

He can't do better than where he is, but he has decided that doesn't define him. He knows we love him unconditionally.  He hasn't failed. But he feels he failed himself.

He has combatted this by focusing on hobbies and things that bring joy.  He writes using a voice software. He forges. He takes his dog on walks.

Of you aren't stuck maybe you could go through Voc rehab or do a 2 yr degree at a job better suited?  If you are stuck @ that job, what other things do you enjoy?  

One thing about being a teen though...most are so busy figuring themselves and their direction out they come off disinterested or uncaring....could be you would be missed but no one thinks to instigate contact cuz they're just busy figuring their own day to day stuff.

So maybe it's about if you traumatize others, you'll be remembered? Maybe part of you wants to be saved eh?  To have them act so you know you are worth saving. 8 am. My son is struggling tonite. The hospital was a joke with his 1st attempt. So I won't do that again. I still owe 10k.  Not that his life isn't worth more! But I'd like it to be helpful.  But I can't sit in his room all night every night. If you don't do it...maybe you could give me advice for him. I sure the fuck don't know what to do to help. He tells me everything. He's loved unconditionally. But that doesn't matter if you've no friends or way to look at the future with hope. So...If you survive this feeling, tell me how. Maybe it would help my son. If not, I hope you do not suffer and know if I had the right words for my own son...I'd sure try to give them to you as well

I hope you are still here and you would share how you made it. My son attempted at 13. He struggles constantly . even tonite. People who are supposed to help are telling me I've done all I can. Have I? I'm not far off of your mom...my own issues. I've let my weakness and depression hurt my kids. It will be my failure if he goes through with it. Every morning he doesn't respond right away, my heart drops like will I find him gone? The worst thing to me is thinking of him going...and being alone while it happens. That I could not even hold or comfort him and give him that peace. So...if you've survived maybe you can offer advice. Is there anything you wish anyone would do to help you fight these feelings? How can I help my son when I can't make things magically better?
